clue.text: Hunt answer round island, northern Taiwan location

indicators.note: the chase word is wrapped round the island and northern letters

parts.note: to hunt is to chase

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for a solution circles an island somewhere in northern Taiwan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts IN (island, northern) inside CHASE, giving CHINASE, and A for answer follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The waters around Taiwan belong to the East and South seas named after the mainland nation, so the island sits in that sea.

clue.text: Rough cowl on top of Borderer's chimney

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a cowl is a monk's hood
LUM is the Scots and northern English word for a chimney, as used on the Scottish Borders

explanation.surface: A cowl perched on top of a chimney somewhere on the Scottish border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' is a noun here: a rough is a thug. A chimney cowl is a real fitting, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, as a noun, is a violent lout or thug, just as a hoodlum is.

clue.text: No way out: only rely on unwinding after noon

indicators.note: the scrambled words come after the noon letter
unwinding suggests something coming loose, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone trapped with no exit, after midday, can only rely on unwinding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way' looks like part of the surface, but it is the definition; 'unwinding' scrambles OUT ONLY RELY ON, set after N.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquial refusal meaning certainly not, equivalent to an emphatic never.

clue.text: Sharp movements upward had shown the way between someone's legs

indicators.note: in a down clue, upward means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: darts are sudden quick movements
'd is the contracted form of had
to have shown the way is to have led

explanation.surface: Someone moving sharply upward after showing the way, perhaps squeezing between another's legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upward' turns DARTS into STRAD in this down clue; 'had' gives D as in the contraction I'd.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sat astride, with a leg on each side, lies between the rider's legs.

clue.text: Utmost effort to look at unfinished passage

parts.note: giving one's all is making an utmost effort

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the synonym is lopped off

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Making the utmost effort to inspect a corridor that hasn't been completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last E of EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow passage between buildings is a lane or alleyway.

clue.text: Quarry sparsely affected by equally spaced depletions

indicators.note: removing letters at equal intervals leaves only every other letter of sparsely

explanation.surface: Hunted game that has thinned out after regular culls.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of 'sparsely' to leave the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarry is an animal being hunted, the victim of a predator.

clue.text: Quivers with ecstasy but for the first time shows regret

indicators.note: but for means except, so the first letter is removed when it matches

parts.note: tremors are quivers or shakes
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone shaking with ecstasy for the first time later feels sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but for the first time' removes T, the first letter, from TREMORS; 'with' joins E for ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep sorrow or guilt over a wrong one has done is a form of contrition.

clue.text: Jerk's name occurring in noisy conversation

indicators.note: the name letter turns up inside the chatter word

parts.note: yak is chatter, noisy talk

explanation.surface: A fool's name keeps coming up in loud gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' tempts as a fool, but it is the verb-like noun: a sudden pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp pull, a tug, is called a jerk.

clue.text: Swear-word, Anglo- Saxon oath cut short in ancient city

indicators.note: both swear words lose their last letters, being clipped at the end

parts.note: damn is a mild swear word
AS is the abbreviation for Anglo-Saxon
a cuss is an oath or curse

explanation.surface: Cursing with a coarse Old English oath, broken off mid-word somewhere in an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' clips the last letter of DAMN and of CUSS, leaving DAM + AS + CUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Syrian capital is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.

clue.text: Anonymous twins' dynamic range

indicators.note: dynamic means energetic and moving, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Two unnamed siblings show a lively range of talents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' is not about ability: it is a line of mountains in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain chain in New South Wales, Australia, highest on that continent.

clue.text: More likely to accept party who's taken a ward?

indicators.note: the comparative word takes in the party word

parts.note: apter is the comparative of apt, meaning more likely
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone more willing to welcome a party guest who has become a guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' is the container signal; 'apter' is a rare but valid comparative of apt, and the question mark flags the definition as an example of an adopter.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has legally taken on a child as their own, as a guardian takes a ward.

clue.text: Handle love on the rebound for rail worker

indicators.note: rebounding sends things back, so the two words together are read backwards

parts.note: handle is slang for a name
love is nil in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Someone getting over a broken romance with a railway employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rebound' reverses the whole run NAME + NIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway employee who maintains or inspects track is a track worker of this title.

clue.text: Routine, drifting ways do in everyone Noah rescued

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go inside the Noah phrase

parts.note: those Noah rescued were in the ark

indicators.note: drifting means wandering about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Animals drift in the Flood while Noah saves everyone on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifting' scrambles WAYS DO into DAYSWO, which goes inside IN ARK (where Noah rescued the animals).
explanation.definitionFit: An expression for something ordinary, a normal part of one's job, as routine is.

clue.text: What's just outside the scope of acts?

definitions.text: What's just outside the scope of acts?

parts.words: What's just outside the scope of acts?
parts.note: just here means legally right, and acts are statutes, so this is lawful practice not set down in Acts of Parliament

explanation.surface: Something fair that falls outside a set of rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' reads as merely but means legal, and 'acts' are parliamentary statutes.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of law built from judges' precedents, as opposed to statute, so it sits beyond Acts.

clue.text: Caterers' work showed fashion sense, perhaps, involving stylised gun

indicators.note: the fashion phrase takes in the scrambled gun

parts.note: someone with fashion sense was hip, so this gives was hip

indicators.note: stylised means reshaped artistically, so the letters of gun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A caterer's fashionable outfit includes a stylish replica gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stylised' is the anagram signal; the surface's fashion sense is part of the wordplay, while the definition is kitchen work after a catered meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning dishes after a meal is a chore of caterers.

clue.text: Irish girl's mother, the first one

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
in Genesis Eve is the first woman

explanation.surface: An Irish girl's mother is the first one in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish female forename, borne by the legendary queen of Connacht.

clue.text: Learn complicated information in Bavarian university town

indicators.note: complicated means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Gaining tricky knowledge at a German college town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges LEARN; GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A city near Nuremberg in Bavaria, Germany, home to a well-known university.

clue.text: Quiet trio leading irregular gathering

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: the leading three letters of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: Three people at the front of an untidy assembly call for silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trio leading' takes the first three letters of 'irregular'. 'Gathering' is the dressmaking sense, not a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: In sewing, rows of stitching pulled up to gather fabric decoratively are this.

clue.text: Stylish woman's attractiveness to be passed genetically?

parts.note: in means fashionable
her is the possessive for a woman
it is sex appeal

explanation.surface: Whether a chic woman's charm can be handed down in her genes.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive traits from parents, as through genes, is to be the heir to them.

clue.text: Spending set out to cover small impediments retrospectively

indicators.note: looking back means the whole construction is read backwards
the laid word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: laid as in laid out, set out
rubs are obstacles, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: Expenses laid out to deal with minor obstacles after the event.
explanation.walkthrough: LA(S RUBS)ID is reversed by 'retrospectively' to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying out money, as from a fund, is an outlay.

clue.text: "Boerewors," perhaps a bit of South African vocabulary?

parts.note: usage is how words are used, here vocabulary

explanation.surface: Boerewors may be a bit of South African slang.
explanation.walkthrough: Boerewors is a coiled South African farmer's sausage; the surface treats it as a word, the definition as a food.
explanation.definitionFit: Boerewors is a spiced coiled meat link from South Africa, an example of this.

clue.text: Manoeuvre withdrawn nobleman into unexpectedly filling AIDS charity receptacle

indicators.note: the reversed peer and scrambled word fill the charity's letters

parts.note: THT is the Terrence Higgins Trust, a British AIDS charity

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests something out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A lord who has retired drops something into an AIDS charity collection box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' turns PEER into REEP; 'unexpectedly' turns INTO into OINT; THT is the Terrence Higgins Trust, a UK AIDS charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A driving move turning a car round in a narrow road in three movements.

clue.text: This might be cubic capacity

definitions.meaning: in maths a cubic is raised to the third, an exponent

explanation.walkthrough: 'cubic capacity' reads as engine size, but 'cubic' is the maths sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube is a number to the third exponent, and capacity means ability or might.

clue.text: Probably a canine lover sat on dog's tail

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a fan is a lover or devotee

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A dog lover sits on the dog's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' is the tooth, not the dog. The tail of 'dog' is G.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine tooth is a long pointed tooth, as is the type in question.

clue.text: Recall most of tungsten containing iodine essential for ventilation

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the iodine letter
to recall is to call back, so the word is reversed
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: wolfram is another name for tungsten
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Remembering most of a metal with iodine inside is key to keeping a room fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: Tungsten is also called WOLFRAM; 'most of' drops M, 'Recall' reverses to ARFLOW, and 'containing' takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Movement of air through a space is needed for ventilating it.

clue.text: Strained expression similar to "bittersweet"?

definitions.meaning: a twisted face showing pain or disgust
grim (bitter) followed by ace (sweet, excellent) imitates the shape of bittersweet

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: GRIM for bitter and ACE for sweet, side by side like 'bittersweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A contorted face, like a wince or scowl, is a strained expression.

clue.text: Last of jazz greats regularly seen in the forefront?

definitions.text: Last of jazz greats regularly seen in the forefront?

indicators.note: the alternate letters stand in front of the jazz letter
regularly takes every other letter of greats
the final letter of jazz is taken

explanation.surface: A jazz great often seen at the front of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan Getz was a celebrated American jazz saxophonist; the whole clue both builds and describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor saxophonist Stan of that surname was a jazz star in the forefront of his art.

clue.text: Prancing to Pride's

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Prancing to Pride's' is cut short: TO PRIDES is anagram fodder for the answer, but the definition is missing and no scan or search gives it.
